learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic structure of a production company and can explain it.
They can name different organizations of company and production systems and classify them into various systematizations.
They can name and describe the essential tasks of production organization.
They know the three main processes in a company: Design to Operate, Lead to Cash, and Plan to Produce (including related processes) and can specifically explain their interfaces.
They know the different process patterns STO, ETO, CTO, CTO+, MTO, MTS, and ATO.

They are able to show how product structures and bills of materials for production are created and how the information network in digitized companies, which must be provided for production, is to be executed.
They know the tasks and methods of modern work preparation and can evaluate them.

Students can present the essential tasks and methods of production planning and control, as well as their mapping in ERP systems, against the background of modern technologies such as Digital Design & Supply Chain Management, Industrial Data Science, AI, etc.
Furthermore, students can derive the necessary measures for automated production monitoring.
Students can sketch and explain the necessary IT architectures for production.

Students utilize the content and possibilities of modern quality management by applying the learned methods and tools so that they can later assess and evaluate the relationships in the product life cycle regarding quality aspects.

They understand that preventive quality management is an essential lever for a successful customer-supplier relationship by successfully conducting discussions and engaging employees to later evaluate, initiate, and implement measures.

syllabus_topics: Production systematics & organization of production companies
Information systems in companies (ERP, PLM and MES)
Types, systematizations and modeling of product structures & bills of materials
Process planning and work plan creation
Technological process chains (e.g. CAD-CAM-CNC process chain)
Production controlling & data acquisition in production

Quality management and its significance / context to synchronous production system / product-process-company quality / quality costs / key figures and policy deployment / standardization and standards / QM in the life cycle / QM methods (especially A3, 8D) / error management / statistics in QM context / audits
teaching_methods: Use of typical production software (e.g. SAP, MES systems)
